name: Steinberg am Rofan
kurzbeschreibung: Tiny village in the district of Schwaz at the foot of the Rofangebirge, offering breathtaking views of Achensee.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Steinberg am Rofan is situated in the Tyrolean district of Schwaz at an altitude of 1,010 metres above sea level in a secluded, sun-drenched high valley northeast of Lake Achensee within the Rofan Mountains (Brandenberg Alps). Framed by the limestone bastions of the Guffert (2,195 m) and the twin peak of the Unnütz (2,078 m), Steinberg is home to around 300 residents, making it the smallest independent municipality in the Schwaz district while encompassing an expansive territory of nearly 69 square kilometres. As an officially certified Bergsteigerdorf (Mountaineering Village) under the Alpine Convention, Steinberg stands for gentle, eco-conscious alpine tourism free from through-traffic, large-scale hotels, or noisy lift complexes. The 19th-century Bavarian author Ludwig Steub famously praised the valley as 'The most beautiful end of the world'. With traditional mountain farms, flowered meadows, and crystalline streams, Steinberg is a sanctuary of unspoilt alpine tranquillity.

Geschichte

Human presence in the Steinberg valley reaches back to antiquity: at the nearby Schneidjoch pass, enigmatic Raetic rock inscriptions dating from the 5th to 4th centuries BC (carved in the North Etruscan alphabet) attest to ancient hunting and ritual sanctuaries. The first documented record dates to 17 June 1188, when Bishop Heinrich of Brixen consecrated the village church dedicated to Saint Lambert of Maastricht. From the 16th to the 19th centuries, Steinberg served as an essential hub of timber provision for the royal salt works: logs felled in local forests were floated along the Steinberger Bach and Brandenberger Ache streams down to Kramsach and onward to heat the salt pans in Hall in Tirol. The parish church of Saint Lambert rests on 12th-century Romanesque foundations with a late-Gothic core, enriched with baroque altars and Gothic fresco fragments during the 18th century. In September 2021, Steinberg am Rofan was formally inducted into the prestigious international network of Mountaineering Villages.

Anreise

By car, Steinberg is accessed from the south via the Inntal motorway A12 (Wiesing/Achensee exit), following the Achenseestraße B181 past Maurach to Achenkirch. From the north, toll-free travel is available from Bavaria via Bad Tölz and the Sylvenstein reservoir or from Tegernsee across the Achen Pass to Achenkirch. At Achenkirch, turn onto the picturesque, ten-kilometre Steinberger Landesstraße (L221), which winds through a forested gorge up into the open mountain valley (the sole access road). Rail passengers arrive at Jenbach railway station in the Inntal valley, where ÖBB Railjet, ICE, and WESTbahn trains stop. From Jenbach station, VVT regional bus route 4080 runs via Maurach and Achenkirch directly to Steinberg am Rofan village centre (Gemeindeamt/Kirche stop).

Tipps

For mountaineers and climbers, the prominent limestone double peak of the Guffert (2,195 m) is the undisputed local icon: its south face offers legendary multi-pitch alpine climbing routes, while the demanding normal hiking route rewards sure-footed hikers with a 360-degree panorama stretching from the Karwendel to the Hohe Tauern. Long-distance trekkers pass through Steinberg on Stage 8 of the famed Tiroler Adlerweg (Eagle Walk). History enthusiasts can embark on a hike to the Raetic rock inscriptions at Schneidjoch, a heritage monument of European significance. In winter, the peaceful valley transforms into a paradise for cross-country skiers and snowshoers: over twenty kilometres of groomed, sun-drenched tracks (classic and skating) crisscross the snowy basin. Ski tourers enjoy uncrowded ascents up the peaceful slopes of Angerberg and Schackenkopf.
